hook: Last video's quiz answer: six thousand rupees. Eight thousand, minus the claim of two thousand. Well done if you got it!
Now, C B S E Class Eleven. T. S. Graywaal, Question thirty-eight.
This trial balance has a trap: purchases adjusted.
So where does closing stock go? Let's solve it together.
question: Here is the question. The trial balance of Ashok, as on thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.
Debit side: building, purchases adjusted, salaries, bad debts, wages, rent, prepaid rent, insurance, furniture, drawings, debtors, and closing stock.
Credit side: capital, sales, wages outstanding, provision for depreciation on furniture, apprentice premium, and creditors.
Both sides total six lakh rupees.
Notice three items in green: purchases adjusted with closing stock, wages outstanding, and prepaid rent. Their adjustments are already done.
adjust: One. Salaries for March, twenty twenty-six, of one thousand rupees were unpaid. And the balance included eight hundred rupees paid in advance.
Two. Insurance is prepaid to the extent of two thousand rupees.
Three. Depreciate furniture by ten percent on original cost, and building by five percent.
Four. Stock of one thousand five hundred rupees was taken by Ashok for his personal use.
Five. Make a provision for doubtful debts equal to ten percent of sundry debtors.
Pause the video, and try it yourself. Then check with me.
already: First, the big trap. Items that are already adjusted.
Purchases adjusted means opening stock, purchases return and closing stock are already adjusted in purchases.
So in the trading account, we show only adjusted purchases. No opening stock, and no closing stock.
Closing stock is inside the trial balance, so it goes only to the assets side of the balance sheet.
Wages outstanding and prepaid rent are also inside the trial balance. Their entries are already passed.
So wages outstanding goes only to liabilities, and prepaid rent only to assets. Do not adjust them again!
a1: Salaries in the trial balance, five thousand. Add outstanding salaries, one thousand. Six thousand.
Less salaries paid in advance, eight hundred. Five thousand two hundred goes to profit and loss.
In the balance sheet, outstanding salaries of one thousand is a liability, and prepaid salaries of eight hundred is an asset.
a2: Insurance, five thousand, less prepaid two thousand. Three thousand goes to profit and loss.
And prepaid insurance, two thousand, is an asset in the balance sheet.
a3: Building at five percent. One lakh fifty thousand into five, over hundred. Seven thousand five hundred.
Furniture at ten percent on original cost. Sixty thousand into ten, over hundred. Six thousand.
Total depreciation, thirteen thousand five hundred, goes to profit and loss.
Furniture has a provision for depreciation account. Twelve thousand plus six thousand makes eighteen thousand.
In the balance sheet, furniture is sixty thousand, less provision eighteen thousand. Forty-two thousand.
And building is one lakh fifty thousand, less seven thousand five hundred. One lakh forty-two thousand five hundred.
a4: Adjustment four. Goods taken for personal use.
Ashok took stock of one thousand five hundred. Deduct it from purchases adjusted. Two lakh eighty-eight thousand five hundred.
And add it to drawings. Five thousand plus one thousand five hundred. Six thousand five hundred, deducted from capital.
a5: Adjustment five. Provision for doubtful debts.
Ten percent of debtors. Twenty-five thousand into ten, over hundred. Two thousand five hundred.
Debit profit and loss: bad debts two thousand, plus new provision two thousand five hundred. Four thousand five hundred.
In the balance sheet, debtors twenty-five thousand, less provision two thousand five hundred. Twenty-two thousand five hundred.
trading: Now the trading account of Ashok, for the year ended thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.
To purchases adjusted, two lakh ninety thousand. Less goods taken by Ashok, one thousand five hundred. Two lakh eighty-eight thousand five hundred.
Credit side. By sales, five lakh twenty-nine thousand five hundred. And no closing stock here!
Gross profit, two lakh thirty-one thousand rupees.
pl: Next, the profit and loss account.
By gross profit, two lakh thirty-one thousand. By apprentice premium, five hundred. Total, two lakh thirty-one thousand five hundred.
Debit side. Salaries, five thousand two hundred.
Bad debts and provision, four thousand five hundred.
Rent, five thousand. Insurance, three thousand.
Depreciation. Building, seven thousand five hundred. Furniture, six thousand. Total, thirteen thousand five hundred.
Net profit, two lakh three hundred rupees.
bs: Finally, the balance sheet of Ashok, as at thirty-first March, twenty twenty-six.
Capital, thirty thousand. Add net profit, two lakh three hundred. Less drawings, six thousand five hundred. Two lakh twenty-three thousand eight hundred.
Sundry creditors, twenty thousand. Wages outstanding, eight thousand. Outstanding salaries, one thousand.
Liabilities total, two lakh fifty-two thousand eight hundred.
Assets. Building, one lakh forty-two thousand five hundred. Furniture, forty-two thousand.
Closing stock, forty thousand. Sundry debtors, twenty-two thousand five hundred.
Prepaid rent, three thousand. Prepaid salaries, eight hundred. Prepaid insurance, two thousand.
Assets total, two lakh fifty-two thousand eight hundred. The balance sheet tallies!
traps: Four exam traps from this question.
Trap one. Purchases adjusted: no opening stock and no closing stock in the trading account. Closing stock goes only to the balance sheet.
Trap two. Wages outstanding and prepaid rent are inside the trial balance. Show them only in the balance sheet. Never adjust them twice.
Trap three. Furniture depreciation goes to the provision account. Show furniture at cost, less the total provision of eighteen thousand.
Trap four. Goods taken for personal use. Deduct them from purchases, and add them to drawings.
recap: Gross profit, two lakh thirty-one thousand.
Net profit, two lakh three hundred.
Balance sheet total, two lakh fifty-two thousand eight hundred, on both sides.
Remember: if it is already in the trial balance, show it only once.
